- F-291 **With the bound `Any`, the compiled path compiles, loads and runs generics at tuple and arrow static arguments as it does with `extends Any` written; `()` fails whatever the bound (row 339), and so does a generic dotted method with one tuple-typed parameter (row 832).** Measured once: generic functions, objects and traits, dispatch to a generic arm and `typecase`, at a pair or an arrow, with the static argument written or inferred. The class loader made the same classes by name, and the program jars read the same under `javap`, as the same programs with `extends Any` written under the compile command's bound `Object`. So the switch to the bound `Any` costs the run time no work for these shapes; its test cost is F-292. Not run: the one library's own instantiations at tuples, tuples of three or more and nested ones, generic functional methods at a tuple, a native that receives a tuple. With `extends Object` written, they are refused, or pass unchecked where the static argument is written (row 470); the compile command's bound is `Any` (`Shell.java:372`). No gated test. Detail: `perf-probes/bound-any-compiled/REPORT.md`, "The shapes by setting" and "What the class loader makes".

- F-38 **The compiled dispatcher chooses an overload arm generic in a size by the value's size, and the arm reads its size.** Called with an argument typed `Any`, the dispatcher reads the size off the value's descriptor. The checker's return-type rule compares the arms' own sizes (row 410). The dispatcher skips a size parameter's bound (`compiler/OverloadSet.java:1501-1502`). Gated by `compiler_tests/NatRtDisp`, `NatRtDispSize` and `NatRtDispTrait`. Detail: `perf-probes/nat/size-probes.md` section 2.

- F-55 **Static arguments are inferred with coercion on both paths: the compiled checker from the arguments' static types and the expected type, walk from their run-time types.** So a mixed-width call takes the narrowest type into which its arguments convert, as P-74 decides. F-73 gives the checker's rule and F-137 walk's; F-87 lists where the checker has an expected type. Under walk, a typed binding converts a call's result after the call and does not fix the call's static arguments: `a: BoxK[\ZZ64\] = wrapK(3)` infers `T` from `3` as `Int` and is refused, since no coercion converts a `BoxK[\Int\]` (row 510). A parameter with no written bound is bounded by `Any` on both paths, so a parameter that nothing fixes takes `Any` (F-78). Gated by `compiler_tests/InferCoercionShapes` and `tests/InferCoercionRungK`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-inference-checker/REPORT.md` section 3.2; `compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/REPORT.md` sections 2 and 9.

- F-129 **A size is carried at run time as a descriptor from `RTTIsize.of`, and a program whose sizes are known at compile time loads, dispatches and runs compiled, apart from the open cases below.** It builds P-41. Each size value, such as the 3 of `Vec[\3\]`, has one descriptor; in a run-time subtype test, it is a supertype only of an equal size. A size read as a value is a constant that the class loader replaces by the numeral. Closures and tasks capture a size as a free static parameter (F-135). A size made from a number known only at run time does not run compiled: `tests/NatReflectTest.fss` stops at load (row 307). Gated by `compiler_tests/NatRt*`. Also open on the compiled path: a `ZZ32Vector` passed to a generic constructor fails at load (row 408); a dispatched overload arm whose static parameter has a concrete generic bound stops the compile in its sized form and dies at load in its type form (row 413); an object that extends two instantiations of one trait, one at a static parameter, passes the checker and dies at load (row 414). Row 416 is walk's defect: walk refuses at load `g(b: Tg[\3\])` beside `g(b: Tg[\4\])`, which the compiled run dispatches, since walk's overloading check applies no exclusion of instantiations. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-size-runtime/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 9.

- F-274 **Under walk, two declarations whose declared domains are equal are refused by the No Duplicates Rule, where one has static parameters of its own and the other has its own or none, whether or not the parameter-by-parameter check orders them.** The parameter check reads a type parameter as strictly below its bound. So it orders `h[\T extends Number\](x: T, y: T)` before `h(x: Number, y: Number)`, though their declared domains are equal. Walk compares the declared domains, each declaration's over all its own instances, and refuses the pair: "fails because their parameter lists have the same types" (F-257). A type parameter bounded by `Any` counts: walk refuses `g[\T\](a: T)` beside `g(a: Any)`, and so does the compiled checker, 'There are multiple declarations of g with the same parameter type: T' (row 759; `compiler_tests/XXXNoDuplicatesRuleUnboundedBesideAny.test`). Gated by `tests/GenericBesideGenericSameDomain`, `GenericBesidePlainSameDomain`, `NoDuplicatesRuleWalk` and `NoDuplicatesRuleSizeWalk` (refused). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-walk-generic-pairs/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 5; `compile-ladder/rung-existential-reduction/REPORT.md` section 5 (row 759 on both paths).

- F-281 **The compiled checker checks the overloading of every operator, symbolic ones included; with them checked, the distance and the count are 0, with no crash (F-53).** Its three loops, over the top-level set, a trait's provided methods and their overriding return types, read `isCheckedName`, which admits every operator (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/OverloadingChecker.scala:766-773`); the export check reads every operator too, each under its declared name only (F-287). An on-demand import adds an api's declarations once, and leaves out a name its `except` clause lists; the check still reads an on-demand api's declaration of a name the component imports by name from another api (row 813), and an `except` that lists an operator leaves it imported on both paths (row 814). Outside its trait, a self type whose `comprises` clause lists types at a `where`-clause variable is read as the trait type (`TypeAnalyzer.selfComprised`), so `AnyList`'s `||` is checked; such a program still stops in the code generator (row 812; row 701). So the distance stage is the full check of F-245. Gated by `compiler_tests/XXXSymbolicOperatorOverloadUnrelated`, `ComprisesWhereFunctionalMethodChecker`, `XXXComprisesWhereFunctionalMethodBounds`, `OperatorPrefixInfixImport` and `ImportExceptOverload`, and by the stages ('#total 0', '#crash none'; '#total 0'). Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-symbolic-check/REPORT.md` sections 1, 3 and 5.

*************)

(************************************************************
* Reductions
************************************************************)

trait Reduction[\L\]
    getter reverse():Reduction[\L\] = ReversedReduction[\L\](self)
    empty(): L
    join(a: L, b: L): L
end

object ReversedReduction[\R\](r:Reduction[\R\]) extends Reduction[\R\]
  getter reverse():Reduction[\R\] = r
  getter asString():String = "ReversedReduction(" || r.asString || ")"
  empty():R = r.empty()
  join(x:R,y:R):R = r.join(y,x)
end

(** Invariants:
    join must be associative with identity empty
    unlift(lift(x)) = x
 **)
trait ActualReduction[\R,L\] extends Reduction[\L\]
    empty(): L
    join(a: L, b: L): L
    lift(r: R): L
    unlift(l:L): R
    (** If this reduction left-distributes over r, return a pair of
        reductions with the same lift and unlift **)
    leftDistribute[\K\](r: ActualReduction[\R,K\]): PossibleReductionPair[\K\] =
        distribute(r)
    (** If this reduction right-distributes over r, return a pair of
        reductions with the same lift and unlift **)
    rightDistribute[\K\](r: ActualReduction[\R,K\]): PossibleReductionPair[\K\] =
        distribute(r)
    (** If this reduction distributes over r, return a pair of
        reductions with the same lift and unlift **)
    distribute[\K\](r: ActualReduction[\R,K\]): PossibleReductionPair[\K\] =
        NoReductionPair[\K\]
end

trait PossibleReductionPair[\R\] extends Condition[\PossibleReductionPair[\R\]\]
    comprises { NoReductionPair[\R\], SomeReductionPair[\R\] }
end

object NoReductionPair[\R\] extends PossibleReductionPair[\R\]
    getter holds(): Boolean = false
    cond[\G\](t:PossibleReductionPair[\R\]->G, e:()->G): G = e()
end

trait SomeReductionPair[\R\] extends PossibleReductionPair[\R\]
    getter holds(): Boolean = true
    getter outer(): Reduction[\R\]
    getter inner(): Reduction[\R\]
    cond[\G\](t:PossibleReductionPair[\R\]->G, e:()->G): G = t(self)
end

trait ReductionPair[\R,L\] extends SomeReductionPair[\L\]
    getter outer(): ActualReduction[\R,L\]
    getter inner(): ActualReduction[\R,L\]
end

(** The usual lifting to Maybe for identity-less operators **)
trait AssociativeReduction[\R\] extends ActualReduction[\R,Maybe[\R\]\]
    empty(): Nothing[\R\] = Nothing[\R\]
    join(a: Maybe[\R\], b: Maybe[\R\]): Maybe[\R\] =
        if av <- a then
            if bv <- b then
                Just[\R\](simpleJoin(av,bv))
            else
                a
            end
        else
            b

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The record's tool: it owns the form of FACTS.md and POSITIONS.md and of
their two history files, and is the only way to write them.
An entry is one line under a permanent number, `- F-87 **Title.** Text.` in
explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md and `- P-48 **Title.** Text.` in
POSITIONS.md. A number is never reused or changed: a new entry takes the
highest number its file has ever used, plus one. An entry stands under the
nearest `## ` or `### ` heading above it, its section. Its title is its bold
opening, or where it has none, its opening words up to the first colon,
semicolon or full stop.
A pointer is another entry's number in the sentence that needs it, alone
(`It builds P-48.`) or with the first words of the target's title in quotes
(`It builds P-48, "A type parameter the arguments do not fix ..."`, or
`P-48 ("...")`). Quoted words must open the target's current title (`...` or
`…` marks words left out); when an entry is retitled, the tool rewrites them
in every entry that points to it, in the same call.
The history (FACTS-history.md, POSITIONS-history.md beside the record) holds,
under `### F-87`, one block per change, oldest first: one provenance line (the
UTC time from the clock, the kind of change, `from` each report section,
`commit`, `by`, then the note after a colon), and the line as it stood before
the change. The tool derives the kind: `added`, `rewritten`, `moved to "S"`,
`merged into F-n`, `F-n merged in`, `removed`, `noted`; the numbering wrote one
`numbered` block per entry. A retitle that refreshed other entries' pointer
words, or a merge that moved their pointers, says so in one more line of the
block (`pointer words refreshed in: F-12, P-48`).
A `noted` block, which `note` writes, leaves the entry as it is. It adds what
the entry's history lacks, such as the curator's messages behind a text kept
word for word, with their times, or a correction of an earlier block. It holds
no earlier line, and its note says what it adds, so it needs one. A gone entry
takes none: its last block stays `merged into` or `removed`. A noted block
that corrects an earlier block names it by its time, in the field after the
kind: `correcting the block of 2026-10-13 19:07Z`, or, where blocks of the
entry share that minute, `correcting the 2nd block of 2026-10-14 04:41Z`,
counted oldest first. The block corrected is never edited.
